blocks.text: Stoichiometry is derived from Greek words stoicheion means element and metron means measure. Collectively, stoichiometry means quantitative measure of reactants and products.

blocks.title: Stoichiometry
blocks.text: Stoichiometry (pronounced as stoy-key-om.eh-tree) is the branch of chemistry in which the relationship between the amounts of reactants and products in a balanced chemical equation is studied.

The balanced chemical equation has the same number of atoms of each type on both sides of equation. It has definite ratios of reactants and products just as compounds have definite ratios of elements. Such ratios are used to calculate the mass or mole of other substances.

Stoichiometric calculations obey law of conservation of mass and law of definite proportions. According to the law of conservation of mass, “matter (mass) can neither be created nor destroyed”. It states in terms of stoichiometry that the total mass of reactants is equal to the total mass of products in a balanced equation. According to the law of definite proportions, a pure compound always contains the same element combined in the same ratio by mass.
Concept of Mole

blocks.title: Mole
blocks.text: The mole is the amount of a substance which contains as many elementary entities as there are atoms in 0.012 kg (12 g) of carbon-12.

The elementary entities may be atoms, molecules, ions, electrons, and other particles. It is represented by n. The number of entities present in one mole of a substance is a constant number named Avogadro’s Number, i.e. 6.02 x 10²³. It is represented by Nₐ. This value is attributed to an Italian scientist Amedo Avogadro (1776-1856).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The scientist’s name is printed “Amedo”; it is Amedeo Avogadro.

blocks.title: Did you Know?
blocks.text: Avogadro’s number is a physical constant representing the molar number of entities. The exact value of it is 6.02214179 x 10²³ mol⁻. In calculations we use the rounded off value 6.02 x 10²³.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The unit is printed “mol⁻” with the power missing; it is mol⁻¹ (per mole): 6.02214179 x 10²³ mol⁻¹.
Examples are given below:

items: 1 mole of ¹²C contains 6.02 x 10²³ atoms of ¹²C.
1 mole of H₂O contains 6.02 x 10²³ molecules of H₂O.
1 mole of NaCl contains 6.02 x 10²³ formula units of NaCl.
1 mole of Na⁺ contains 6.02 x 10²³ ions of Na⁺.

blocks.text: The chemists use the mole as the SI unit to weigh and count atoms, molecules, formula units or ions.

The mass of one mole of a substance (element, compound or ionic species) is equal to the atomic mass, molecular mass, formula mass or ionic mass of a substance when expressed in grams and is known as molar mass, represented by M.

blocks.title: Molar mass
blocks.text: The mass of one mole of a substance expressed in grams is called molar mass.
The unit of molar mass is g/mol. The molar mass is the sum of the masses of the component atoms.
The mass of one mole of CCl₄ can be found by adding the masses of carbon and chlorine present.

blocks.latex: \begin{aligned}\text{Molar mass of }\ce{CCl4} &= \text{Molar mass of one C} + \text{Molar mass of Cl} \times 4\\ &= 12.0 \times 1 + 35.5 \times 4\\ \text{Molar mass of }\ce{CCl4} &= 12.0 + 142.0 = 154.0\ \text{g}\end{aligned}
blocks.text_alt: Molar mass of CCl₄ = Molar mass of one C + Molar mass of Cl x 4 = 12.0 x 1 + 35.5 x 4; Molar mass of CCl₄ = 12.0 + 142.0 = 154.0 g

blocks.text: Other Examples

items: 1 mole of carbon atoms is 12.0 g.
1 mole of CO₂ molecule is 44.0 g.
1 mole of CaO formula units is 56.1 g.
1 mole of CO₃²⁻ ions is 60.0 g.

blocks.text: The number of moles of a substance can be calculated by dividing mass in grams by molar mass. The formula for number of moles is:

blocks.text_alt: Number of moles = Given mass / Molar mass

blocks.title: Sample Problem 4.1
blocks.problem: Calculate the number of moles present in 20 g of NaOH.
steps: Number of moles = Given mass / Molar mass

blocks.title: Sample Problem 4.2
blocks.problem: Calculate the mass of 0.5 moles of HCl.
steps: Mass of HCl = Number of moles x Molar mass

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Sample Problem 4.2 asks for a mass, so the unit is grams: 0.5 x 36.5 = 18.25 g (about 18.3 g), not 18.3 mol.

blocks.title: Sample Problem 4.3
blocks.problem: Calculate the mass of 10⁻³ mol of MgSO₄.
steps: Molar mass of MgSO₄ = 24 + 96 = 120 g mol⁻¹
blocks.answer: Mass of MgSO₄ = 10⁻³ mol × 120 g mol⁻¹ = 120 × 10⁻³ = 0.12 g
